# Transportation Impact Brief: Rachel (Disruption-Averse Parent)
## PERSONA-008 | South Portland FY27 Budget Analysis

---

## Executive Summary

The three configurations under consideration are not equivalent in their disruption to children and families. Option A would split 139–169 elementary families across two buildings — 18–24% of all elementary families — and create a care gap affecting 42–144 households at an annual family cost of $144K–$804K, exposure the district did not model before advancing the proposal. Option B produces zero split families, zero care gap, and zero new route expansion cost. The board voted on Option A before the transportation routing work was complete.

---

## Key Finding

**Under Option A, between 139 and 169 families would have children assigned to different school buildings.**

That is 18–24% of elementary families — not an edge case, not a rounding error. Under Option B, that number is zero. The difference is not administrative convenience; it is the measure of how many children lose their shared school community.

---

## Configuration Comparison

| Metric | Option A | Variant C | Option B |
|---|---|---|---|
| Split families | **139–169** | 123–150 | **0** |
| Split families as % of elementary | 18–24% | 16–21% | 0% |
| Care gap families | 42–144 | 37–128 | **0** |
| Family-borne care cost (annual) | $144K–$804K | $127K–$714K | **$0** |
| Bus tiers required | 3–4 | 3–4 | 3 |
| SEA driver shortfall | −10 to −13 | −9 to −12 | −4 to −7 |
| Route expansion cost | $748,472 | $623,726 | **$0** |
| Total fiscal exposure | $946K–$1.68M | $797K–$1.45M | $30K–$80K |
| Fiscal exposure as % of claimed savings | 43–112% | 36–97% | 1.4–5.3% |

*Source: SPEC-060 through SPEC-065. FY25 baseline. Family costs are not district costs — they are borne by households.*

**Note on the 4th bus tier:** Option A and Variant C may require a 4th routing tier due to grade-band reassignment. The current driver idle window (9:30 AM–1:30 PM) leaves no room for a 4th tier without overtime. A 4th tier also creates a 30-minute scheduling gap that directly affects split families — the households least able to absorb it.

---

## What's Missing

The district has not published the following analysis, despite the decisions being live:

- **No transition plan exists on record.** The routing work was described as "underway with partner" at the March 30, 2026 board meeting — operationalized *after* the board vote, not before. No document specifies how split-family logistics will be managed during the transition year.
- **No care-gap mitigation plan.** After-care is already full at 4 of 5 schools. Only Kaler — the school slated for closure — has openings. The district has not identified how families who currently rely on Kaler's after-care capacity will be accommodated.
- **No bell schedule proposal for a 4-tier system.** If Option A requires a 4th tier, the operational constraints (driver idle window, overtime cost, SEA contract terms) make this non-trivial. No bell schedule has been published.
- **No redistricting criteria.** Parents have asked which schools, which grades, and which children. The administration has not provided written criteria for how students would be assigned under any configuration.
- **No educational impact analysis.** Fiscal modeling was presented; learning continuity, class placement, and social-emotional impact were not.

*Sources: TC-003, TC-006, TC-007, TC-009, TC-011; SPEC-062, SPEC-063, SPEC-064.*

---

## Limitations

This analysis quantifies disruption by configuration but cannot tell you:

- Which specific children would be split. The 139–169 figure is a modeled range, not a named list.
- Whether the district's routing partner will find a 3-tier solution for Option A that avoids the 4th tier. If they do, the care-gap figure shrinks.
- What the actual SEA driver staffing level will be post-cut. The range (−10 to −13 for Option A) depends on which positions are eliminated, which has not been finalized.
- Whether before/after care providers could expand capacity to absorb displaced Kaler families. The $144K–$804K family cost estimate assumes no new capacity is created.

The driver shortfall exists under **every configuration**, including Option B (−4 to −7 drivers). This is a baseline operational problem independent of which restructuring option the board selects.

---

## Invitation to Improve

The district can narrow the uncertainty ranges in this brief by providing:

1. **The routing model output** — routes, stops, and tier assignments for each configuration
2. **A bell schedule proposal** for any configuration requiring a 4th tier
3. **The before/after care capacity assessment** — enrollment, wait lists, and expansion feasibility at each receiving school
4. **The redistricting criteria** — written, not oral, specifying how student assignments would be made
5. **A transition timeline** — including when families would be notified, how placement preferences would be gathered, and what appeals process exists

This brief will be updated when that data is published. The district is invited to submit corrections or clarifying data for incorporation.
